intent: To illustrate the demographic proportions of Sunni and Shia Muslims and the friction between these groups.

requirements.question: Must the video state or visualize Sunni as 80% of the Muslim-world whole, or is a relative bar height enough?
Must the video state or visualize Shia as 20% of the Muslim-world whole, or can it be shown only as the remainder?
Does the video need an explicit majority/larger-than label, or is the visible 80-versus-20 order sufficient?

units.claim: Sunni Muslims make up about 80% of the Muslim world.

basis.note: Table value is 80; narration frames it as about 80% of the Muslim world.

accept: Sunni Muslims make up about 80% of the Muslim world.
The Sunni share is approximately 80 percent.
80% of the Muslim world is Sunni.
units.evidence: A Sunni-labeled mark must occupy about 80% of the whole, e.g. an 80% bar/area/slice or four-fifths of the composition.

units.claim: Shia Muslims make up about 20% of the Muslim world.

basis.note: Table value is 20; narration frames it as about 20% of the Muslim world.

accept: Shia Muslims make up about 20% of the Muslim world.
The Shia share is approximately 20 percent.
20% of the Muslim world is Shia.
units.evidence: A Shia-labeled mark must occupy about 20% of the whole, e.g. a 20% bar/area/slice or one-fifth of the composition.

units.claim: Sunni Muslims are the larger group and Shia Muslims are the smaller group.

basis.note: 80 is greater than the Shia value of 20.
20 is less than the Sunni value of 80.

accept: Sunni share is higher than Shia share.
units.evidence: The Sunni visual element must be clearly larger or higher than the Shia visual element.

optional_valid: The combined Sunni and Shia shares total 100% (80 + 20 = 100).
The Sunni-Shia gap is 60 percentage points (80 - 20 = 60).
Sunni share is four-fifths and Shia share is one-fifth.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded
